product.amstrad-alt-286.summary: The entry-level ALT with the same VGA screen as the 386SX.
product.amstrad-alt-286.history: Amstrad introduced the ALT-286 at CeBIT in March 1990 as the lower-priced of its two ALT laptops. Micro News reported a planned June release in France at 16,770 francs before tax. In July 1991, Amstrad Germany offered it with a portable Canon BJ-10e printer for 4,600 marks.
product.amstrad-alt-286.technical.storag: Storage specifications vary by source. The manual lists a 20 MB hard drive and a 1.44 MB internal floppy drive. The Centre for Computing History lists 60 MB and 720 KB for its CH46565 specimen.
product.amstrad-alt-286.technical.bios: The manual identifies the two boot firmware chips. U302 and U303 are TMS27C256 EPROMs with Amstrad part numbers 270386 and 270387.
product.amstrad-alt-286.technical.verifi: The factory configuration and board schematic have been cross-checked. The BluMach sheet remains in research.
product.amstrad-alt-286.technical.limita: The system BIOS and U508 video ROM still need to be dumped. Boot and LCD control remain to be validated in BluMach.
product.amstrad-alt-286.technical.photo: In the Zaragoza museum photograph, the ALT-286 is to the right of the IBM PC.
